name: Richard Burton

Schoolmaster Philip Burton became his mentor, adopted him, and guided his theatrical training. He made his professional debut at 18, served in the RAF (1944-47), then launched his film and stage career with critically praised performances by his early twenties.
family_context_summary: Born the 12th child of a Welsh coal miner in Pontrhydyfen; mother died when he was 2 and he was raised by his eldest sister in Taibach. Working-class family with no theatrical tradition, but Philip Burton, a schoolmaster, adopted and mentored him.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family theatrical tradition. However, schoolmaster Philip Burton became his legal guardian, adopted him, and provided intensive dramatic training and mentorship, effectively replacing his biological family's domain with theatrical education.

name: Robert Huber

name: Steve Ballmer
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Microsoft in June 1980 at age 24 as its 30th employee and first business manager, receiving $50,000 salary and 7% equity; by late 1981 (age 25) he helped secure the landmark IBM deal to outfit all new PCs with MS-DOS, one of the most consequential deals in tech history.
early_history_summary: Born in Detroit, Ballmer was a first-generation college student who graduated magna cum laude from Harvard in 1977 with a degree in applied mathematics and economics. He worked at Procter & Gamble for two years, briefly attended Stanford MBA program, then joined his Harvard classmate Bill Gates at Microsoft in 1980, becoming the company's first business manager and securing the pivotal IBM partnership within his first year.
family_context_summary: Born in Detroit, Michigan; father worked as a manager at Ford Motor Company. Ballmer was a first-generation college student who attended college prep classes at Lawrence Technological University in high school.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a Ford Motor Company manager, providing a middle-class upbringing and exposure to corporate management. No direct tech industry family background.

name: Nils Liedholm

He earned 18 caps for Sweden, winning Olympic gold in 1948, which led to his transfer to AC Milan.
